chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Indeed, the Opening of the Book [Surah Al-Fatihah] alone suffices in the obligatory [prayer]."

This is understood to apply in a state of necessity, as indicated by what we mentioned earlier, that it is not permissible to restrict oneself to Surah Al-Hamd alone when choosing freely, and what clarifies this further is what he narrated:

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book, referring to Surah Al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: Is Surah Al-Fatihah alone sufficient for the obligatory prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that while Surah Al-Fatihah alone suffices for the obligatory prayer, this ruling is primarily applicable in cases of necessity (darurah) or when one is unable to recite additional verses. In normal circumstances (ikhtiyar), the standard practice requires reciting Al-Fatihah along with another Surah or portion thereof, ensuring the completeness of the recitation component. This distinction highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence between the minimum requirement and the recommended perfection of prayer.
